questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Mass of a Thin Rod
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/ca0ff396606039accf8c3acb4fd1b8e505dd16d2fe9b765fcd5c043d1538a573.png)

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=2{x}^{3}\,\text{kg/m},$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?
questions.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the  $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b,$ if $\lambda (x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by      

$$
m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=2{x}^{3},\,a=0,\,b=2.
$$

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{4}}{2}-0 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $8\,\text{kg}.$

questions.problem: The mass density function $\lambda ,$ measured in $\text{kg/m},$ of a thin rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le 2$ is given by $\lambda (x)=3{x}^{2}+1,$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?
questions.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b,$ if $\lambda (x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by  

$$
m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=3{x}^{2}+1,\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

  

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{1}^{2}3{x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{3}+x]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =({2}^{3}+2)-({1}^{3}+1) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $8\,\text{kg}.$

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{kg/m},$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?
questions.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the  $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b,$ if $\lambda (x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by      

$$
m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=\frac{8}{{x}^{3}},\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}8{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-4{x}^{-2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & ={[-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-(\frac{4}{4}-\frac{4}{1}) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $3\,\text{kg}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Moment of a Rod About the Origin
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/7f88ca365b75320795e9d38170a8586399d759696638a4bd78c73ca6c6f44b1a.png)

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=4-x\,\text{kg/m}.$ Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=4-x,\,a=0,\,b=3.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{3}x\cdot (4-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}4x-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =(2\cdot {3}^{2}-\frac{{3}^{3}}{3})-0 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $9\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$

questions.problem: A thin rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)=6x,$ measured in $\text{kg/m},$ is placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le 2,$ where $x$ is measured in meters. Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=6x,\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot 6x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot ({2}^{3}-{1}^{3}) \\  & =14\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $14\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$

The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

$$
\lambda (x)=4{x}^{2},\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot 4{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{4}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{4}-{1}^{4} \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A thin rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)=3x+1,$ measured in $\text{kg/m},$ is placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le 2,$ where $x$ is measured in meters. Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=3x+1,\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot (3x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}3{x}^{2}+x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(8+\frac{4}{2})-(1+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{17}{2} \\  & =8.5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $8.5\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Center of Mass of a Rod
questions.problem: Consider a thin rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $0\le x\le 2$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)=3x.$ Given that the rod's mass is $6$ units, what is the $x$-coordinate of its center of mass?
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass, denoted $\overset{―}{x},$ of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=3x,\,a=0,\,b=2.
$$

So, the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot 3x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =8-0 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{8}{6}=\frac{4}{3}.
$$

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=x+{x}^{2}.$ Given that the mass of the rod is $\frac{5}{6}$ units, what is the $x$-coordinate of its center of mass?
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=x+{x}^{2},\,a=0,\,b=1.
$$

So,  the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot (x+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{7}{12})}{(\frac{5}{6})}=\frac{7}{10}.

questions.problem: Consider a thin rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le e$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)=\frac{1}{x}.$ Given that the rod's mass is $1$ unit, what is the $x$-coordinate of its center of mass?
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass, denoted $\overset{―}{x},$ of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=\frac{1}{x},\,a=1,\,b=e.
$$

So, the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\text{d}x \\  & ={[x]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =e-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{e-1}{1}=e-1.
$$

questions.problem: Consider a thin rod along the $x$-axis over the interval $0\le x\le 4$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)=\sqrt{x}.$ Find the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass of the rod.
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=\sqrt{x},\,a=0,\,b=4.
$$

So, the mass of the rod is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot {4}^{3/2}-0 \\  & =\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{4}x\cdot \sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2}{5}{x}^{5/2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot {4}^{5/2}-0 \\  & =\frac{64}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{64}{5})}{(\frac{16}{3})}=\frac{12}{5}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
The thin rod below has the mass density function $\lambda(x) =2x\, \textrm{kg/m},$ where $x$ is measured in meters. What is the total mass of the rod?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/8c8386ff979b46cd994f1ace60f681a6590856e6960e7d74c71a29bb3f0f2d1a.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Given a thin rod oriented along the  $x$-axis over the interval $a \leq x \leq b,$ if $\lambda(x)$ denotes the mass density function of the rod, then the total mass of the rod is given by      

$$
m = \int_a^b \lambda(x) \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\lambda(x) = 2x, \qquad 
a=1, \qquad 
b=3.
$$

We calculate the mass of the rod as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{1}^{3} \\  & ={3}^{2}-{1}^{2} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the rod is $8\,\textrm{kg}.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Moment of a Rod About the Origin
canonical_examples.problem:
The thin rod below has the mass density function $\lambda (x) = (x+4)\,\textrm{kg/m}.$ Find the moment of the rod about the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/7f88ca365b75320795e9d38170a8586399d759696638a4bd78c73ca6c6f44b1a.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda(x)$ for $a \leq x \leq b$ is given by 

$$
M_O = \int_a^b x\, \lambda(x) \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x) = x+4, \qquad 
a=0, \qquad 
b=3.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{3}x\cdot (x+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}+4x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+2{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}+2\cdot {3}^{2})-0 \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $27\,\textrm{kg}\cdot \textrm{m}.$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040800/assets/461c4cb760541ea435620803689e193d13c9cb4706a59b031d37da6ffd49ab9f.png)

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x) = x^3.$ Given that the rod's mass is $4$ units, what is the $x$-coordinate of its center of mass?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a \leq x \leq b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda(x)$ is given by 

$$
\overline{x} = \dfrac{M_O}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $\displaystyle m = \int_a^b \lambda (x) \: \textrm{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- $\displaystyle M_O = \int_a^b \, x\lambda (x) \: \textrm{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x) = x^3, \qquad 
a=0, \qquad 
b=2.
$$

So,  the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(32-0) \\  & =\frac{32}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\overline{x}= \dfrac{M_O}{m} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{32}{5}\right)}{4} = \dfrac{8}{5}.
$$

 

Note that this result makes intuitive sense. Since $\lambda$ is an increasing function of $x,$ we would expect the center of mass to be located closer to the right endpoint and further from the left endpoint.
